description: Two adults who were sexually abused as children by former Boston police officer and Boston Police Patrolmen's Association president Patrick Rose Sr. filed a federal lawsuit on June 8, 2023 against the City of Boston, former police commissioner Paul Evans and more than a dozen other officials and institutions, including the police union and the Massachusetts Department of Children and Families. Rose pleaded guilty in April 2022 to 21 counts of child rape and sexual assault involving six children and is serving a prison sentence with a 10-year minimum. The suit alleges that officials knew of a 1995 abuse complaint against Rose that an internal investigation sustained, yet allowed him to remain on the force and rise to union president while he continued abusing children, and that their handling of a DCF investigation put the plaintiffs in greater danger, including by allegedly interviewing a child victim within view of Rose and discouraging re-interviews. A district judge dismissed the case in March 2024, but on July 25, 2025 the First Circuit partially reversed in Doe v. City of Boston, ruling the plaintiffs plausibly alleged state-created-danger claims, and remanded. On remand the city asserted qualified immunity, with a hearing set for late October 2025; no resolution had been reported as of July 2026.
